thread:
jon: Heads-up — strict schema validator in eu-west started rejecting a lot of fncall/tool responses around 11:02 UTC. We're seeing a big bump in fallbacks and quota churn. https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/validators :eyes:

mira: Ugh. Any error samples? which routes affected?

jon: Quick tail from the metrics stream:
```
validator.rejects{region=\"eu-west\",route=\"nlp-parse\"} = 1240 (1m)
fallback.count{route=\"nlp-parse\",variant=\"degen\"} = 1112 (1m)
quota.spike{account=acct-42} = +8% (billing)
```

sam: Can you run this query against the ingest logs to get the top rejection codes?
```
SELECT code, count(*) FROM validator_events WHERE region='eu-west' AND ts > now()-5m GROUP BY code ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;
```

lina: Reminder: strict-validate fncall was in a canary — we set it to 5% for canary last week. Did something change in rollout?

deploy-bot: rollout.change: user=admin updated rollout strict-validate-fncall region=eu-west percent=50 -> 11:01:22 UTC

mira: omg that explains it. Who bumped it to 50%? That should never be manual without a runbook. :grimacing:

carol: We should also tag telemetry with reject_reason and validator_version. Right now reject counts are opaque, makes debugging and dashboards painful. Suggest the metric: validator.rejects_by_reason{reason,version,route,region}.

jon: For immediate mitigation: 1) reduce canary back to 5% or 0% in eu-west 2) add alert: if (rejects / requests) > 0.2 && fallback_count > 100 -> page 3) attach sample payloads for top 3 reasons to S3 for triage.

lina: I'm toggling permissive for eu-west now (short-lived) — will follow up with a rollback if traffic stabilizes.

sam: Command I used: `redwoodctl rollout update --feature strict-validate-fncall --region eu-west --percent 5`

deploy-bot: rollout.updated: strict-validate-fncall region=eu-west percent=5 requested_by=lina 11:05:09 UTC

mira: Also UX ask for Console: expose per-route validator toggle + a sampling slider (0-100%) with an audit log that shows who changed it and why. Right now it's too buried. :+1:

carol: Longer-term: soften failures with a soft-reject path that emits a metric but allows response with a warning header. That would avoid quota spikes while preserving signal. We can add a per-route policy: hard-reject | soft-flag | permissive.

jon: Agreed. Filing follow-up ticket and assigning triage/metrics work. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INF-9876 — assign to @sam and @carol.

sam: I'll take metrics/dashboards. I'll add a panel for reject_rate, fallback_rate, and reject_reason top-5, 1m granularity and an alert rule.

lina: I'll add a small Console PR for the toggle visibility and audit log link — low risk UI change.

jon: Thanks team. We'll post a short postmortem if this ends up billing-affecting customers. :heart:
